title: Faith and love give ability as habitual gifts
source_text: XIV. Quae vero dicit de posse, quod per fidem & charitatem datur, de donis istis habitualibus potissimum intelligenda monet: quoniam per illa dicuntur justi orare, diligere, bene vivere, tentationesque superare posse, etiam quando nihil istorum agunt. Quandoquidem sunt virtutes in animo permanentes, quae hoc ipso robustum animum efficiunt, ad opera quaedam peragenda, quamvis si adhuc imperfectae sint, ad opera sublimioris ordinis non sufficiant.
pass_a_gloss: XIV. But what he says of being able, which is given through faith and charity, he warns is to be understood chiefly of those habitual gifts: since through them the just are said to be able to pray, love, live well, and overcome temptations, even when they do none of these things. Since they are virtues abiding in the soul, which by this very thing make the soul robust, for performing certain works, although if they are still imperfect, they do not suffice for works of a more sublime order.
pass_b_english: Thesis XIV. What he says about the ability given through faith and love, he cautions, should be understood chiefly of these habitual gifts. Through them the righteous are said to be able to pray, love, live rightly and overcome temptations even when they are doing none of these things.
For they are virtues that remain in the soul and so make it strong enough to carry out certain works, though while still imperfect they are not enough for works of a higher order.

lemmas.gloss: for works of a more sublime order

choices.why: Kept as in the earlier grace loci: habitual gifts abide; actual grace is a passing motion.

bible_refs: Cornelius Jansenius, Augustinus (Louvain, 1640), tome 3, De gratia Christi Salvatoris.
